summary: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe specializes in computational studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at Tohoku University (~1972–1975) and served there as an assistant (1975–1990), professor at the Institute for Materials Research (1990–2012), professor emeritus (2012), and senior research fellow (2018).

Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1957–1987) and as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (~1977–1987).

Youru Wang works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Temple University under supervisors Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 1999) and Rowan University (attested 2007, 2018).
Youwei Kang was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from around 1891 to 1898, where he taught Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1991–1996), he held positions at St. Thomas University, Japan (~2005–2008), Shitennoji University (~2008–2012), Sophia University, and Tohoku University (~2013).

Yu Daoquan worked in Tibetology and linguistics, studying at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1936). He was a professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China from 1953 to 1992.
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Tsui completed master's studies at Columbia University supervised by Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller (attested 2018), and had Sheng Yen as a traditional teacher.

Yu-kwan Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University (PhD ~1980–1985 under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara). Ng held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~1995–2011).

Yu-min Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee held a post as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002) and taught Pei-jung Wu.
Yuan Ren is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and as a researcher at the Institute of Chinese Buddhist Culture.

Yuanying was a Buddhist studies figure who served as abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan Temples, and as councilor and president of the Buddhist Association of China. He also founded and served as president of the Yuanming Lengyan School (1945).

Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp along with advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.

Yuen Ren Chao was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Cornell (~1910–1914) and Harvard (~1915–1918). He held posts at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua (~1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.
Yuguang Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and later served as the university's president from around 2011 to 2015.
Yui Chi Lau was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yingguang Qu, founded the Vajrayana Esoteric Society, and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland (attested 2012).
